claims.statement: The HAAP directory is a phone book, not a notary: agent identity lives in the agents' Ed25519 keys (fingerprint HF-<16 hex> derived from the key), and the directory only indexes signed manifests and verifies endpoint control; it is not an identity authority, so a compromised or malicious directory can hide or poison discovery results but cannot impersonate an agent, and clients should re-verify the agent's /.well-known/haap.json directly.

haap/registry.py implements the directory as a reference in-memory service with zero runtime dependencies beyond the stdlib: RegistryStore keeps listed agents and pending challenges in dicts guarded by a single threading.RLock, RegistryServer wraps it in an http.server ThreadingHTTPServer, and every process restart starts with empty state; the entry TTL is configurable per store instance via RegistryStore(entry_ttl=...).

docs/DIRECTORY_SERVICE_BRIEF.md is an implementation brief, not implemented code in this repository: it scopes a separate production-grade HAAP Public Directory (haap/directory_service package and haap-dird CLI, SQLite-backed, /v1 routes, rate limits, audit, geo and pagination search) that must stay wire-compatible with registry.py and registry_client.py, which the brief says remain untouched with the unmodified tests/test_registry.py and tests/test_registry_client.py as the acceptance bar; the repo README points production operators to a separately operated directory (https://acoalex.com/haap-directory, github.com/acoalex/haap-directory).

Registry defaults are ENTRY_TTL_S = 24*3600 (an entry expires without a heartbeat), CHALLENGE_TTL_S = 60 (proof-of-endpoint window), and MAX_AGENTS = 10_000 (anti-flooding cap); tests exercise expiry by constructing RegistryStore with a 2-second entry_ttl instead of sleeping for the real TTL.

RegistryStore.submit_registration performs all server-side verification before issuing any challenge: manifest.agent.fingerprint must match ^HF-[0-9a-f]{16}$, the base64-decoded public key must hash (SHA-256, 16 hex chars) to that fingerprint, the manifest signature must verify with KeyPair.verify_with over canonical JSON, and manifest.agent.endpoint (trailing slashes stripped) must start with http:// or https://; any failure returns (False, message) surfaced as HTTP 400, and success only stores a pending challenge (nonce, issued time, verified key) keyed by fingerprint — the agent is not listed at this step.

All manifest signatures in the directory ecosystem are computed and verified over exactly json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode(); the same canonical form is used by registry.py verification, by registry_client.build_registration when signing, and is mandated unchanged by the production brief.

A successful POST /register returns 200 with challenge_nonce plus registry_fingerprint and registry_signature, the latter being the RegistryServer's own generated KeyPair signing the nonce's ASCII bytes, so an agent could verify it reached the intended directory before completing; the reference registry_client checks only for challenge_nonce and does not verify the registry signature.

RegistryStore.complete_registration is single-use and expiry-checked: it pops the pending challenge before validating, so any completion attempt for a fingerprint consumes its challenge and a failed or expired completion forces the agent to restart at POST /register; it then rejects on challenge age above CHALLENGE_TTL_S, on a caller-supplied public key differing from the submit-verified key (when supplied), or on an endpoint proof that fails verification, and on success writes the record {manifest, registered_at, last_seen, endpoint_proof (first 64 chars), endpoint_nonce} and lists the agent.

Proof-of-endpoint binding is enforced against the key retained in the pending challenge at submit time: verify_endpoint_proof checks KeyPair.verify_with(raw_pub, nonce.encode("ascii"), proof) over the stored key, and the HTTP /register/complete handler never forwards the public_key_b64 the client also sends, so the store-level key-equality check only applies to direct store callers; a proof signed by a different key leaves the agent unlisted, pinned by test_failed_endpoint_proof_not_listed.

Re-registering an already-listed fingerprint is an update, not a duplicate: complete_registration overwrites self._agents[fingerprint] with a fresh record (registered_at and last_seen refreshed), so RegistryStore.count() stays 1 after repeated full registrations of one agent (test_duplicate_registration_updates).

Heartbeat in the reference implementation is an unauthenticated liveness renewal: heartbeat(fingerprint) refreshes last_seen only for a currently live record and returns a bool, and HTTP POST /heartbeat {fingerprint} answers 200 {status: ok} or 404 {status: unknown}; no timestamp or signature is checked at this layer, whereas the signed heartbeat contract (signature over heartbeat:{fingerprint}:{timestamp} within a ±300 s window) belongs to the production service specified in the brief.

Entry expiry in RegistryStore is lazy and logical: a record is alive iff now - last_seen <= entry_ttl, and get returns None, heartbeat refuses, and search/count skip records past that threshold, but no code path removes records from the _agents dict (there is no physical pruning), so reads filter rather than reclaim memory.

The MAX_AGENTS cap is enforced only inside submit_registration and only for fingerprints not already in the dict (len(_agents) >= MAX_AGENTS and fp not in _agents); because expired records are never removed, the comparison counts every distinct fingerprint that ever completed a registration in this process, and re-registration of any previously registered fingerprint is always admitted via the update path.

The HTTP surface of RegistryServer: GET /health returns 200 {status: ok, agents: <alive count>}; GET /search?capability=X&q=Y returns 200 {results: [...]}; GET /agents/{HF-<16 hex>} returns 200 with the stored manifest or 404 {error: not registered or expired}; other GET paths return 404 {error: not found}; POST bodies are parsed as JSON from the Content-Length header and non-JSON input yields 400 {error: invalid JSON}.

Search semantics of RegistryStore.search: capability is a case-insensitive substring match against agent.speciality plus every manifest tools[] name and skills[].name, and q is a case-insensitive substring over the JSON of the whole manifest; results are the stored manifests themselves (never server records with proofs or timestamps), returned in the {results: [...]} envelope.

RegistryServer identity and serving mechanics: each server generates its own Ed25519 signing KeyPair when none is injected and derives its fingerprint from it; start(host='0.0.0.0', port=8444) binds a stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer whose serve_forever runs on a daemon thread with daemon request threads, returns the HTTP server object (port 0 gives an ephemeral port used by tests), and stop() shuts it down.

registry_client.register drives the full two-round-trip flow: build_registration returns (manifest, public_key_b64, manifest_signature) built from capabilities.public_manifest and a canonical-JSON signature; register POSTs those to /register, raises DiscoveryError (code DISCOVERY_FAILED) if no challenge_nonce comes back, signs the nonce's ASCII bytes with the agent's private key, POSTs /register/complete with {fingerprint, manifest, endpoint_proof, public_key_b64}, and returns the response only when it carries status == "registered"; network failures raise DiscoveryError for an unreachable directory.

registry_client.search returns the parsed results list of manifests from GET /search and heartbeat returns True exactly when the server answered {status: ok} for POST /heartbeat {fingerprint}; the shared _request helper parses 4xx JSON bodies instead of raising so protocol rejections surface as parsed responses rather than exceptions.

HeartbeatLoop is the agent-side keep-alive daemon: start() spawns a daemon thread that posts a heartbeat every interval_s (default DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_S = 6*3600, well below the 24 h entry TTL so an entry cannot expire between beats), records the last outcome on last_ok (False on DiscoveryError), and stop() sets a threading.Event to end the loop.

CLI wiring for the registry family in cli.py: haap registry serve constructs a plain in-memory RegistryServer and blocks until Ctrl+C then stops cleanly (default host 0.0.0.0, port 8444); registry register loads the local IdentityStore identity and requires a declared endpoint (HAAPError otherwise) before calling registry_client.register with the speciality; registry search calls registry_client.search and prints fingerprint, speciality, name and endpoint per match; errors funnel into main's HAAPError-to-exit-code-2 contract.

The reference directory behavior is pinned end to end over real HTTP (tests boot RegistryServer on 127.0.0.1 with port 0): tests/test_registry.py covers full proof-of-endpoint registration followed by search and profile fetch, bad-signature and fingerprint/key-mismatch rejection, wrong-key proof leaving the agent unlisted, duplicate registration updating in place, heartbeat renewal with expiry at a 2 s TTL, and capability/free-text search; tests/test_registry_client.py exercises the unmodified registry_client register/search/heartbeat against a live directory.
